title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
authors: Tatsuya Kaneko, Ritsuki Hirabayashi, Yutaka Akagi
abstract: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.
summary: This theoretical study uses DMRG on a Kondo ladder model to examine magnetic correlations in the presence of an on-site Coulomb interaction (U). The authors find that U enhances antiferromagnetic correlations even when the noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting that electron-electron interactions can drive magnetic instabilities independently of conventional Fermi surface mechanisms.
main_problem: The study investigates how electron-electron interactions enhance antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins in a Kondo ladder system, particularly when the noninteracting electronic structure is gapped.
main_result: A moderate on-site Coulomb interaction (U) enhances AFM correlations for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities even when the underlying noninteracting structure is gapped.
method: The Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) method was employed to calculate spin correlation functions and local magnetizations.
model_or_system: The model is a two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder described by a Hamiltonian including hopping terms, an on-site Coulomb interaction (U), and a Kondo coupling (J_K). The analysis focuses on regimes where the noninteracting system has a narrow indirect band gap.
key_observables: Spin correlation function ($F_{ll'}(r)$), correlation length ($\xi$), and local magnetization ($\langle \hat{S}_{z,l}^{(j)} angle$) induced by a pinning field.
important_parameters: Hubbard interaction strength ($U/t_{\parallel}$), ratio of hopping parameters ($t_{\perp}/t_{\parallel}$), and Kondo coupling strength ($J_K/t_{\parallel}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed at half-filling, and the study contrasts the gapped regime (where RKKY theory fails) with semimetallic regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the noninteracting band structure, the dependence of the correlation length ($\xi$) on $U$, and the spatial profile of the staggered local magnetization induced by a pinning field.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the context of gapped systems where conventional magnetic theories fail. It then uses DMRG to calculate spin correlations, demonstrating that interaction strength $U$ drives the enhancement of AFM correlations. Finally, it links this enhancement to electronic structure changes, such as the redistribution of kinetic energy.
why_interesting: The finding that electron-electron interactions can induce magnetic instabilities in a gapped system, bypassing the need for Fermi surface nesting, provides a novel theoretical mechanism for understanding magnetism in strongly correlated materials.
